query: For high-entropy-alloy protective coatings in wear-resistant applications, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs their wear performance and why? Define a controlled change that would distinguish the hypothesis from a baseline, the directional observations expected if it is correct, the range over which it should hold, the prior evidence that supports it, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing the local lattice-distortion effect in high-entropy-alloy coatings (by adding W) stabilizes the microstructure, promotes second-phase strengthening, and thereby reduces wear rate under pin-on-disk contact conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: A baseline AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating (no W addition) prepared under identical processing conditions.
generation.intervention: Introduce incremental W (e.g., 0.5–1.0 at.%) into the AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating to increase local lattice distortion.
generation.conditions: Perform pin-on-disk tribological tests at room temperature, employing normal loads of 5–40 N and sliding speeds of 0.2–1.0 m/s, with microstructural (SEM/TEM/XRD) analysis before and after wear tests.
generation.structural_mediator: Increased lattice distortion and the formation of W-rich intermetallic phases in the high-entropy matrix.
generation.mechanism: The added W enhances lattice distortion, refining microstructure and improving hardness, which mitigates abrasive and adhesive wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline coating, the W-doped coatings should exhibit lower wear volume loss, reduced friction coefficient fluctuations, and fewer abrasive grooves under identical testing conditions.
generation.baseline: Undoped AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy coating exhibiting higher wear volume loss and more pronounced abrasive/adhesive wear.
generation.boundary: This mechanism is expected to hold for moderate contact loads (up to ~40 N), room-temperature operation, and sliding speeds up to ~1.0 m/s. Extreme temperatures or extended sliding durations remain unverified.
generation.uncertainty: Exact proportions of W and interactions with other elements may require refinement for optimal distortion without inducing brittleness. Extrapolation beyond tested temperature or load ranges is not established.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two sets of AlCoCrFeNi coatings: one undoped and one systematically doped with W up to 1.0 at.%. Conduct pin-on-disk tests under matching loads and speeds at room temperature.
measurements: Coating microstructure via SEM/TEM to track phase formation and lattice distortion
Vickers microhardness measurements before and after wear tests
Wear volume loss and friction coefficient from pin-on-disk tribology tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of W does not significantly alter hardness or microstructure, or if the W-doped coatings do not show reduced wear volume compared to the undoped baseline under the specified test conditions, then the hypothesis is refuted.

cited_evidence.text: In recent years, high-entropy alloy coatings (HEA) have attracted significant attention due to their unique design concept and excellent comprehensive performance [,]. On that basis, the high-entropy ceramics coatings (HEC) are formed by filling nitrogen atoms in the interstitial position of high-entropy alloy coatings, which process a stronger lattice distortion effect which leads to better mechanical properties [,]. Excellent mechanical properties make high-entropy ceramics coatings a potential candidate for wear-resistant materials []. The objective of this study is to investigate how the addition of the lubricating element Mo harmonizes the hardness and fracture toughness and thereafter affects the tribological properties of the material. To do that, a series of (AlCrTiZrMox)N coatings with different Mo contents were deposited using magnetron co-sputtering. The elemental composition, microstructure, mechanical properties, and tribological properties of the coatings were investigated, and the relationship between the wear resistance and the mechanical properties of the coatings was revealed.

AbstractFriction and wear properties of hot working die steel at above 800 °C are of particular interest for high temperature applications. Here, novel AlCoCrFeNiWx high-entropy alloy (HEA) coatings have been fabricated on the surface of hot working die steel by laser cladding. The effects of the as-prepared AlCoCrFeNiWx HEA coatings on the microstructure and high temperature friction and wear behavior of hot working die steel are investigated through scanning electron microscopy (SEM), electron probe microanalysis (EPMA), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS). Having benefited from the formation of W-rich intermetallic compounds after the addition of W elements, the high temperature wear resistance of the coatings is obviously improved, and friction coefficient shows a large fluctuation. The microstructural characteristics of the AlCoCrFeNiWx HEA coatings after the high temperature wear resistance test shows a highly favorable impact on microstructure stability and wear resistance, due to its the strong lattice distortion effect of W element on BCC solid solutions and the second phase strengthening of the W-rich intermetallic compounds. The introduction of W in the AlCoCrFeNi HEA system provides a potential solution for high temperature application because of its high melting point, low coefficient of thermal expansion, and good creep resistance [,]. More specifically, the introduction of W does not change the original phase composition of HEA []. Therefore, the performance of AlCoCrFeNi HEA is expected to be enhanced via introducing W particles. In this work, the AlCoCrFeNiWx (x = 0, 0.5 and 1) HEA coatings were fabricated by laser cladding on hot working die steel. The morphology of the microstructure and chemical composition of micro-areas were investigated in detail. The wear resistance of the coatings was tested at a high temperature, and then the wear mechanism of the worn surfaces was analyzed.
